prompt: Manufacturers should be legally required to make products that can be repaired easily instead of encouraging consumers to replace them. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is often argued that manufacturers should be legally required to make products that can be repaired easily instead of encouraging consumers to replace them. However, I personally agree with this view because it can reduce environmental waste and help conserve natural resources.

The primary reason why I agree with this view is that making products easier to repair can reduce environmental waste. This is mainly because people can continue using damaged products instead of throwing them away and buying new ones. In other words, repairing products can reduce the amount of unwanted items that end up in landfills. For example, a consumer may repair a damaged smartphone instead of replacing it with a new one. As a result, less electronic waste can be produced and environmental pollution can be reduced. Therefore, I believe that manufacturers should make products easier to repair.

Furthermore, another important reason why I agree with this view is that repairable products can help conserve natural resources. This is because producing new products requires raw materials, while repairing existing products reduces the need for new materials. For instance, if people repair household appliances instead of replacing them, manufacturers may need fewer raw materials to produce completely new products. Consequently, pressure on natural resources can be reduced. Therefore, I strongly agree with this view.

In conclusion, I firmly agree with the view that manufacturers should be legally required to make products that can be repaired easily. This is mainly because it can reduce environmental waste and help conserve natural resources.
